extracted.intended_audience: college administrators, grants officers, and faculty at primarily undergraduate/state colleges
extracted.subtask_description: Survey-based identification of obstacles, motivators, and institutional supports for faculty involvement in grant seeking and grant writing, with concrete recommendations for colleges to foster grantsmanship among faculty.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequency of faculty engagement in grant seeking
rubrics_metrics.description: How often faculty usually engage in grant seeking or grant writing (very often, often, sometimes, rarely, never).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used as a primary activity metric; in the study only 19% reported 'very often' or 'often'. Can distinguish active vs. less active faculty for subgroup analysis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional assistance locating funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which the college provides assistance in identifying or locating potential sources of outside funding (very often, often, sometimes, rarely, never).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: About one-third reported receiving this 'very often' or 'often'; correlated with greater faculty grant activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Released time to prepare proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of released time specifically to prepare a proposal (frequency and perceived importance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported rarely provided; 78%+ indicated released time to work on proposals/grants is highly desired. Recommendation: offer limited released time or speculative proposal development awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Released time to work on successful grants
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of released time to work on grants after award (frequency and importance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported more frequently than release-for-preparation (25% 'very often' for working on successful grants); considered one of the most important motivators.

rubrics_metrics.name: Return of a portion of indirect costs to department
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether departments receive a portion of indirect/administrative costs derived from grants (frequency and importance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rarely reported (4% 'very often' or 'often'); recommended as a way to fund travel, equipment, adjunct replacements, or departmental research funds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personnel support (secretarial help or graduate assistants)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of extra clerical/graduate assistant support for faculty engaged in grant work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 11% reported this 'very often' or 'often'; active grant seekers reported receiving this more. Suggested use of indirect funds to support replacements or assistants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Administrative support (extra funds for travel or equipment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of extra institutional funds for travel or equipment to support grant-related scholarly activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reported by 15% as provided 'very often' or 'often'; considered important by faculty (77% rated as important).

rubrics_metrics.name: Consideration of grants in tenure and promotion
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether grant activity is considered in tenure/promotion decisions (frequency and perceived importance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 41% reported this was provided 'very often' or 'often'; 77% considered it important; institutions should clarify and communicate the role of grants in evaluations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognition in college publications
rubrics_metrics.description: Public recognition of grant activity in college/university publications (frequency).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Most frequently reported reward (61% 'very often' or 'often'); recommended as low-cost but meaningful recognition practice (letters, announcements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Other forms of public recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Non-publication recognitions (awards, announcements, ceremonies) for faculty grant activity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 29% reported 'very often' or 'often'; recommendations include research awards of the year and presidential/provost congratulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Personal financial compensation or stipends
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision of modest monetary rewards (stipends) for successful grant awards or publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Viewed as possible small-cost incentive (e.g., $25–$50) funded by foundations; recommended as symbolic appreciation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Satisfaction of obtaining a grant as motivator
rubrics_metrics.description: Intrinsic satisfaction from obtaining grants (importance as a motivating factor).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 78% rated satisfaction as very important or important; non-financial motivators matter.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to support promising ideas or research
rubrics_metrics.description: Having the opportunity to pursue promising scholarly ideas via grants (importance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 89% rated opportunity and released time as very important or important; institutions should enable faculty to pursue intellectually promising projects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Access to resources to acquire needed equipment
rubrics_metrics.description: Ability to obtain equipment through grant funds (importance as motivator).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 74% rated as important; administrative support to pursue equipment-focused grants is motivating.

rubrics_metrics.name: Building professional reputation
rubrics_metrics.description: Using grant activity to build one's reputation as a capable researcher (importance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 80% rated very important or important; recognition mechanisms and support can reinforce this motivator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy teaching load as obstacle
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which heavy teaching loads prevent faculty from engaging in grant activities (very much, much, somewhat, none).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Overwhelming majority (89%) reported heavy teaching loads as 'very much' or 'much' an obstacle; primary institutional target for change is teaching load reduction or released time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Heavy student advising load
rubrics_metrics.description: Extent to which advising duties prevent grant engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 47% reported as 'very much' or 'much'; suggests need to consider advising relief when offering grant-writing time.

rubrics_metrics.name: Committee and administrative assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: Committee work and other departmental/college assignments as obstacles.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Committee assignments (43%) and other assignments (42%) rated as significant obstacles; streamlining service expectations may help.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of advance warning/late information about opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Receiving information too late to prepare a competitive proposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 40% reported insufficient advance warning; institutions should disseminate opportunities earlier and more effectively.

rubrics_metrics.name: Perception of 'too much work and bother'
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty view that grant activity is too burdensome to be worth effort.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 39% identified this; reducing procedural friction and offering assistance can lower perceived burden.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of knowledge about funding sources
rubrics_metrics.description: Faculty lacking awareness of available funding sources as an obstacle.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 32% reported this; proactive dissemination and training on searching for opportunities recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of training in grant seeking and writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Insufficient skills in proposal development preventing engagement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 31% reported lack of training; recommended remedy: workshops, seminars, individualized assistance, and graduate courses on grant development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of knowledge of budgeting
rubrics_metrics.description: Deficiencies in preparing accurate and adequate budgets for proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 28% reported as obstacle; institutions should provide budgeting training and business-office support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lack of collaborators/colleagues
rubrics_metrics.description: No colleagues with whom to work on proposals as an impediment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 28% reported this; recommendation: facilitate surveys and networking to match faculty with similar interests for collaborative proposals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cumbersome sponsor rules and regulations
rubrics_metrics.description: Sponsor-imposed rules/regulations perceived as a barrier to submitting proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 17% reported as significant obstacle; technical assistance to interpret sponsor rules can mitigate this.

rubrics_metrics.name: Campus proposal review and approval requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Internal campus bureaucratic requirements (multiple signatories/approvals) impeding timely submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Identified as obstacle; recommended careful analysis to eliminate unnecessary signatories and streamline approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance: how to look for grant opportunities
rubrics_metrics.description: Provision and importance of training/help on where and how to find grant opportunities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 34% reported receiving this help often; 84% rated it very important or important. Grants offices should proactively advertise and teach searching strategies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance: how to write competitive proposals
rubrics_metrics.description: Help in learning to write competitive proposals (frequency and importance).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only 15% reported receiving this often, but 82% rated it important; recommended: workshops, one-on-one critique, grant-writing specialists to edit/assist.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance: how to prepare accurate and adequate budgets
rubrics_metrics.description: Training/support in constructing accurate proposal budgets.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 14% reported receiving this often; 80% rated it important. Business-office collaboration and budgeting tutorials recommended.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance: obtaining administrative approvals
rubrics_metrics.description: Help obtaining the necessary campus administrative approvals for proposals.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 25% reported receiving this often; 77% rated it important. Grants offices should guide faculty through internal approvals.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance: dealing with prospective sponsors
rubrics_metrics.description: Assistance in communicating and negotiating with prospective sponsors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 11% reported receiving this often; 77% rated it important. Grants staff should coach or liaise with sponsors when appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Technical assistance: dealing with college business office
rubrics_metrics.description: Help navigating interactions with the college/business office (accounting, administration).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 17% reported receiving this often; 72% rated it important. Strengthen collaboration between grants office and business office.

rubrics_metrics.name: Existence of an operating grants or sponsored research office
rubrics_metrics.description: Whether the college has a functioning grants/sponsored research office and how that affects support provision.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: 80% indicated their colleges had such an office; campuses with offices reported significantly more technical assistance across multiple domains.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants office staffing and roles
rubrics_metrics.description: A fully operational grants office including a grants administrator and grant-writing specialists who assist faculty (not just process applications).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended that staff provide hands-on help (finding sponsors, editing/writing proposal sections); active assistance correlated with greater faculty engagement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Grants/faculty handbook/manual
rubrics_metrics.description: A faculty handbook detailing policies on contact with sponsors, proposal/budget preparation, approvals, PI responsibilities, IP, human/animal subjects, authorized signatories, etc.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Should be distributed to all new faculty; reduces confusion and bureaucratic friction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Proactive and accessible training programs
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer workshops/seminars repeatedly at varied times/locations; pay special attention to female and junior faculty schedules and needs.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In-depth seminars and individualized assistance remove intimidation; accessibility signals institutional commitment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Streamline campus proposal approval process
rubrics_metrics.description: Analyze and reduce the number of required signatories/approvals to speed proposal submission without sacrificing integrity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Removing unnecessary approvers improves efficiency and lowers a major obstacle to timely submissions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allocate funds or policies for released time and adjunct coverage
rubrics_metrics.description: Provide limited released time for proposal development and use indirect cost returns to pay adjuncts or fund replacements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: speculative proposal development awards requiring at least one submitted proposal; use indirect funds to establish research funds or pay adjuncts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reallocate indirect cost returns to support departments and faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Return a percentage of indirect/administrative costs to departments to support travel, equipment, or research activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Can be used to seed departmental research funds or support faculty released time; low-cost way to incentivize grant-seeking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Institutional recognition awards and small stipends
rubrics_metrics.description: Offer non-cash awards (e.g., research award of the year) and modest stipends for successful grants/publications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Low-cost symbolic recognition improves morale and signals value for scholarly activity.

rubrics_metrics.name: Promote collegial and student-inclusive research collaborations
rubrics_metrics.description: Facilitate faculty matching for collaborative proposals and encourage faculty-student grant work.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Develop surveys to identify shared interests and create opportunities for collaborative proposal development.

rubrics_metrics.name: Frequent and clear communication that the institution values grant development
rubrics_metrics.description: Publicly acknowledge submissions and awards (letters from president/provost, campus newspapers, alumni bulletins, trustees minutes).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Regular communication and personal acknowledgement (letters, calls) help create a research-supportive climate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include grant development in graduate curricula
rubrics_metrics.description: Consider adding grant development courses to graduate programs to prepare future faculty to seek funding.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Provides early training for potential faculty and builds a pipeline of grant-competent scholars.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted assistance for junior and female faculty
rubrics_metrics.description: Recognize that junior faculty report receiving less technical assistance and that female faculty place higher importance on assistance; provide targeted outreach and support.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Prioritize technical assistance, mentoring, and scheduling flexibility for these groups to close gaps in access and perceived importance.
